get_market_by_id.description: Retrieves a specific market by its numeric ID and returns that market's details.

get_market_by_slug.description: Retrieves a specific market by its slug and returns that market's details.

get_market_bbo.description: Retrieves current market data for a market by its slug in a lightweight format, returning the best bid/offer and market stats.

get_market_book.description: Retrieves current market data for a market by its slug, returning the order book (bids and offers) and market stats.

get_market_settlement.description: Retrieves the settlement price for a specific market by its slug.

get_price_history.description: Returns book-derived Yes and No display prices over time for one market, identified by its slug passed as `symbol`, for a fixed interval or a custom Unix-timestamp range.

params.name: fixedInterval
params.description: Fixed history window. Do not combine with timestamp parameters. One of: INTERVAL_ALL, INTERVAL_1M, INTERVAL_1W, INTERVAL_1D, INTERVAL_6H, INTERVAL_1H, INTERVAL_LIVE. Pair with fidelity: INTERVAL_1H/INTERVAL_6H/INTERVAL_LIVE use 1, INTERVAL_1D uses 5, INTERVAL_1W/INTERVAL_1M/INTERVAL_ALL use 180.

params.name: timestamp.startTimestamp
params.description: Custom range start in Unix seconds. Requires end_timestamp and cannot be combined with fixedInterval.

params.name: timestamp.endTimestamp
params.description: Custom range end in Unix seconds. Requires start_timestamp and cannot be combined with fixedInterval.

params.name: fidelity
params.description: Fidelity in minutes (minimum 1). Use the documented value for the selected fixed interval, or 1 for a timestamp range.

get_asset_price_history.description: Returns a dense, ascending OHLC candle series per requested asset between from and to, one candle per bucket, used as reference price history for crypto, gold and silver price markets.

params.name: assets
params.description: Assets in canonical <class>:<symbol> form (gateway.types.v1.AssetId), e.g. crypto:btc, commodity:gold or commodity:silver. Repeat the query parameter to request multiple, e.g. ?assets=crypto:btc&assets=commodity:gold. At most 10; duplicates are deduped server-side.

params.name: from
params.description: Unix-seconds start of the window. Aligned down to the bucket, and raised when the window would exceed 3600 candles; the effective start is echoed in AssetPriceSeries.from.

params.name: to
params.description: Unix-seconds end of the window. 0 or a future value means now. The in-progress bucket is included. A past value is aligned up to 10 s for sub-minute buckets, or to one bucket otherwise; the effective end is echoed in AssetPriceSeries.to.

list_series.description: Retrieves all series (e.g., NFL 2025-26 Season) and returns the list of series.

get_series_by_id.description: Retrieves a specific series by its ID and returns that series.

list_sports.description: Retrieves all sports and returns the list of sports.

get_sport_by_slug.description: Retrieves a single sport by its slug and returns it with all its leagues attached.

list_sport_events.description: Retrieves events for a sport by its slug (e.g. 'football', 'basketball') and returns the list of events.

create_order.doc_notes: The order ID returned here is consumed by [get_order](get_order.md), [cancel_order](cancel_order.md) and [modify_order](modify_order.md). Use [preview_order](preview_order.md) first to validate parameters without placing anything. Latency stopgap (from the provider's Rate Limits page): new orders not processed within 5 seconds are rejected with `Order Processing Max Delay Exceeded` (previously `Global Rate Limit Exceeded`). This is a transient latency reject, not a rate limit; the request may be resubmitted.

close_position.doc_notes: From the provider's Python SDK reference (close\_position vs Sell Order, Slippage Tolerance): | | `close_position` | Sell Order (`create`) | | - | - | - | | **Position size** | Entire position | Any quantity | | **Order type** | Market only | Limit or market | | **Use case** | Quick full exit | Partial sells, limit prices | Use `close_position` when you want to fully exit a position at market price. Use a sell order (`ORDER_INTENT_SELL_LONG` or `ORDER_INTENT_SELL_SHORT`) when you need to sell a specific quantity or set a limit price. ### Slippage Tolerance For market orders and close position, you can specify slippage tolerance: Closes the **entire** position at market price. Latency stopgap (from the provider's Rate Limits page): orders not processed within 5 seconds are rejected with `Order Processing Max Delay Exceeded`; the request may be resubmitted.

list_positions.description: Returns the user's trading positions across all markets, or filtered to a specific market, as a map of market slug to position with cost, realized PnL, cash value and decimal quantities.

params.name: market
params.description: Filter positions by a specific market slug. When provided, returns only the position for that market. Example: `will-team-a-win`.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of positions to return per page. Use with `cursor` for pagination. Server default: `100`. Example: `50`.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor` field. Use to fetch the next page of results. Omit for the first request.

list_positions.response_notes: `positions` is a map keyed by market slug (`positions{}` = any key). Fields netPosition, qtyBought, qtySold, bodPosition, qtyAvailable and availablePositions are marked deprecated in the docs; prefer the *Decimal variants.

list_activities.description: Returns the user's account activities (trades, position resolutions, and account balance changes such as deposits and withdrawals), with cursor pagination.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of activities to return per page. Use with `cursor` for pagination. Server default: `100`. Example: `50`.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor` field. Use to fetch the next page of results. Omit for the first request.

params.name: marketSlug
params.description: Filter activities by a specific market slug. Returns only activities (trades, resolutions) related to that market. Example: `will-team-a-win`.

params.name: types
params.description: Filter by activity types; only activities of the selected types are returned. TRADE (order executions), POSITION_RESOLUTION (market settlements), ACCOUNT_DEPOSIT/WITHDRAWAL (fund transfers).

params.name: sortOrder
params.description: Sort order for activities by timestamp. SORT_ORDER_DESCENDING returns newest first (server default), SORT_ORDER_ASCENDING returns oldest first.

list_activities.response_notes: Each activity carries `type` plus one of `trade`, `positionResolution`, `accountBalanceChange`. trade.costBasis and trade.realizedPnl are nullable objects. trade.qty and the non-Decimal UserPosition quantities are deprecated in the docs. Enums: trade.state TRADE_STATE_NEW|CLEARED|BUSTED|INFLIGHT|PENDING_RISK|PENDING_CLEARED|REJECTED; positionResolution.side POSITION_RESOLUTION_SIDE_LONG|SHORT|NEUTRAL; accountBalanceChange.status ACCOUNT_BALANCE_CHANGE_STATUS_PENDING|COMPLETED|PARTIALLY_REFUNDED|REJECTED (all with full prefixes).

get_account_balances.description: Gets the user's current account balances per currency, including current balance, buying power, asset values, open orders, unsettled funds, and pending withdrawals.
get_account_balances.response_notes: Numeric balance fields are documented as `type: number, format: decimal`.

list_incentive_programs.description: Returns active and historical incentive programs grouped by market, each with its time periods (program type, window, reward pool, status, liquidity targets), with page-token pagination.

params.name: page_size
params.description: Number of markets to return per page. Use with `page_token` for pagination.

params.name: page_token
params.description: Pagination token from a previous response's `nextPageToken` field. Omit for the first request.

params.name: symbols
params.description: Filter by market symbols. Returns only programs for the specified markets. Sent as repeated query keys (explode).

params.name: statuses
params.description: Filter by program status: `active`, `closed`, or `pending`. Sent as repeated query keys (explode).

params.name: program_type
params.description: Filter by program type, such as `liquidityProgram` or `volumeProgram`.

params.name: query
params.description: Case-insensitive substring match on market slug.

params.name: instrument_states
params.description: Filter by instrument lifecycle state. Sent as repeated query keys (explode). The doc prose also mentions `INSTRUMENT_STATE_CLOSED`, which is not in the schema enum.

list_incentive_programs.response_notes: instrumentState enum: INSTRUMENT_STATE_OPEN, INSTRUMENT_STATE_PREOPEN, INSTRUMENT_STATE_SUSPENDED, INSTRUMENT_STATE_EXPIRED, INSTRUMENT_STATE_TERMINATED, INSTRUMENT_STATE_HALTED, INSTRUMENT_STATE_MATCH_AND_CLOSE_AUCTION, INSTRUMENT_STATE_PENDING. maxSpread is liquidity-programs only (half-width in price dollars from mid).
list_incentive_programs.auth_note: Concept Notes: the retail incentives schema declares no security for this endpoint; unconfirmed whether signed headers are required. Planned as host=auth (resource is on api.polymarket.us); sending signed headers should be harmless. Confirm with a live call.

list_incentive_earnings.description: Returns the authenticated caller's incentive rewards, each entry summing all payouts for a single market and Eastern Time date, with reward amount, program type and status.

params.name: start_date
params.description: Start date filter (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Server default: the program launch date.

params.name: end_date
params.description: End date filter (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Omit for through-today.
